items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: he knew the Johnsons, he knew the peoples.

ctx.x: I said, "You will not - you are a percussionist." The first time he ran to me and said, "Guess what?" I said, "What are you talking about?" Before he could open his mouth I said, "You're going to play Radio City." He said, "How do you know?" I said, "They're friends of mine." Naturally I was hanging out with Mr. Billy Gladstone and the people at Radio City - that's Wall Street and Mr. Billy Gladstone would

sit and look and hear guys play and he already knew he was the epitome. He was such a flexible man, you see. He knew the peoples that I knew from living in Washington - he knew the Johnsons, he knew the peoples. That's the reason he could understand me. I knew the Chick Webbs and Sid Catletts and what have you, but to know these peoples and to have that background, you see. It was something different, Milt.

Just hold it for a second while I change tape because we got a couple drummers I think we're going to talk about. So you were talking about J. C. Heard and when he joined Cab's band when Cozy had left to go to CBS. John Hammond finally got some things going where they would use some black people -
